transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-02-26 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Evans (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (CSM) -- Dr. Lina Morales (Head of ML, Synergy), Samir Patel (Platform Lead), Emily Chen (Security), Noah Green (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto): renewal check-in, multi-region staging, security/sovereignty notes, pricing follow-up

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda — review current usage, proposed reserved capacity, timeline for EU + APAC staging, and any open security or procurement items. sound good?
[00:18] Dr. Lina (Synergy): yeah that works. we just want to make sure the numbers map to our production peak for the RAG infra — last quarter we saw some spiky loads during nightly indexing jobs.
[00:33] Samir (Synergy): quick note, we currently have about 200M tokens/month committed, with spike bursts hitting roughly 6k rps at peak for small prompt sizes — so when you talk about reserved capacity we need headroom.
[00:49] Priya (Redwood SE): got it, thanks Samir. Priya here — technical point: for latency-sensitive retrieval augmentation we'd recommend Dedicated capacity in EU for the steady-state traffic, with Hosted as the burst/overflow lane. that lets you keep tail latency under 200ms for 512-token interactions.
[01:06] Emily (Synergy): are those latencies from EU edge or from hosted US? because we need to meet SLAs for EU customers and also EU data residency constraints.
[01:20] Priya: the 200ms number is from EU-dedicated pods (we tested on g5-equivalent infra). Hosted US would add network hops, so higher p95. For strict residency we can do Private (VPC) deployment in our EU region.
[01:36] Dr. Lina: Private is attractive but also adds procurement and infra timelines — what's the onboarding estimate?
[01:45] Jordan: typical VPC/on-prem path is 6–8 weeks for initial pilot (VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log forwarding), then another 4 weeks for full activation across routes. for a staged rollout we can do a canary EU pilot in about 4 weeks if the customer is flexible on limited endpoints.
[02:03] Noah (Synergy): procurement flag — cost visibility is critical. if we're doing a 12mo reserved commit what's the uplift for dedicated versus hosted on a per-token basis? can you send a clear pricing table?
[02:16] Jordan: yes, we'll send a detailed grid. short answer: dedicated reserved capacity has lower unit cost for steady throughput; hosted is higher per-token but no infra commit. i'll include an APAC ramp discount in the grid.
[02:30] Samir: can you highlight quantization options? we ran some 4-bit runs in house and saw minimal quality drop but big cost wins.
[02:39] Priya: absolutely — we have quantized model profiles (4-bit, q4f) we can recommend. for RAG workflows we usually pair a quantized base for retrieval scoring and a higher precision fallback for final generations. that's part of the Optimize playbook.
[02:56] Dr. Lina: okay, good. security side — Emily, did you want to say anything about KMS or audit retention?
[03:03] Emily (Synergy): yes. We need envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. retention policy: at least 2 years for logs, and we might ask for 7 years downstream for regulated stuff — that's a hard ask for legal. do you support per-route retention policies?
[03:20] Priya: we do support per-route audit-level logging and forwarding; retention long-term is typically part of the enterprise add-on. we'll note the 2-year requirement and flag the 7-year ask for legal escalation.
[03:34] Jordan: also worth mentioning SSO: we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning and RBAC control planes so your engineers won't need separate creds.
[03:44] Noah: that helps. back to timeline — if we aim to sign a 12mo amendment, what's the earliest EU pilot could be live?
[03:53] Priya: if we get the sanitized prompts and confirm the VPC details quickly, EU canary pilot by mid-May (approx 10 weeks). that's for private VPC. Hosted EU endpoints are faster — like 2 weeks — but won't satisfy full data residency.
[04:08] Dr. Lina: we'd prefer Private for PHI-like clinical metadata even if it's more work. but maybe start with Hosted for secondary workloads.
[04:18] Priya: that matches what other life-sciences customers do — they run non-sensitive batch tasks on Hosted while the sensitive inference goes to Private EU Dedicated.
[04:29] Jordan: can we talk numbers? what are you thinking for committed capacity if we move to a 12-month contract?
[04:36] Samir: initial ask is 500M tokens/month committed with an option to scale to 800M in Q3 if adoption continues. Also an APAC burst region to handle Asia evenings — not full dedicated capacity at first, just a burst pool.
[04:51] Jordan: 500M baseline is reasonable. we'll model pricing for 500M reserved on Dedicated EU with Hosted overflow and the ability to scale to 800M with 30 days notice. i'll include burst pool pricing for APAC.
[05:02] Dr. Lina: for the performance baseline we want Redwood to run the EU tests using our prompt set — specifically the nightly indexing workload and the 50ms SLA-ish interactive queries.
[05:12] Priya: we'll run throughput and latency tests. question — are the nightly index jobs hitting a single large batch (like 4k tokens) or many small requests? that changes batching behavior.
[05:24] Samir: it's a mix — long indexing interactions ~1500 tokens but they only happen a few times; the majority are 32–128 token queries.
[05:34] Priya: thanks — we will simulate both profiles. Priya to run baseline in EU at 2x concurrency to ensure headroom.
[05:42] Jordan: wanted to confirm one more operational detail — do you need guaranteed p99 windows? we can include SLO-based credits for p99 outages as part of the dedicated SLA.
[05:53] Emily: yes — p99 and p95 numbers matter. also need to know how version rollouts work; we want pinned model versions and controlled rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regression.
[06:05] Priya: rollouts: you can pin a model version per-route, and we support canary percent rollouts plus automatic fallback to previous model if evals show regressions. we also surface token-level cost and latency in Console.
[06:18] Dr. Lina: any notes on data retention for inputs/outputs? we keep PII-sanitized payloads for a month internally; do you keep inference logs by default?
[06:28] Jordan: default is short retention for transcript logs; enterprise customers can opt-in for longer retention and into audit forwarding. with Private you can disable server-side retention entirely.
[06:38] Noah: procurement — contract length: is there flexibility for 9 or 18 months, or is 12 standard?
[06:44] Jordan: 12 months is our standard for reserved capacity. we can do 9 but pricing will be slightly higher; 24 gives better unit pricing. we'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[06:55] Samir: are there termination clauses around unexpected burst charges? we prefer predictable billing windows.
[07:01] Jordan: we typically have a committed baseline, and anything above is billed at the overage rate. we can add caps or alerts to help manage churn — and we can include a mutual review clause quarterly.
[07:12] Dr. Lina: let's talk validation — what does Redwood need from us to run the perf tests?
[07:18] Priya: sanitized prompt set, sample payloads, and expected SLA targets (p50/p95/p99). also network reachability for VPC peering if we run private pilot.
[07:28] Dr. Lina: we'll provide that. can you also share the security pack and SOC2 copy?
[07:32] Jordan: yes — Jordan to share security pack link and SOC2 artifact. note: will redact PII in shared docs.
[07:39] (brief cross-talk)
[07:46] Priya: one more thing — for APAC we recommend starting with a burst pool in Singapore region; that'll reduce RTT for APAC by ~60–80ms for interactive prompts compared to US-hosted fallbacks.
[07:58] Samir: good — initial APAC burst of small capacity is fine. we only need dedicated there when we add local regulatory workloads.
[08:07] Priya: also, for cost optimization we can enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts; that can save a lot in high-QPS flows.
[08:15] Dr. Lina: note that our system prompts are fairly static for some flows — caching would help.
[08:22] Noah: procurement question: will you accept a PO (purchase order) model or require a signed amendment + SOW?
[08:29] Jordan: enterprise usually gets a signed amendment + SOW; we can also accept a PO depending on internal legal review. we'll surface options.
[08:37] Emily: security check — do you have SCIM and SAML?
[08:40] Priya: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported, and RBAC mapped to roles.
[08:45] Emily: good. also need to know if logs can forward to Splunk via TLS.
[08:49] Priya: yes, log forwarding over TLS to your SIEM endpoints is supported.
[08:53] Jordan: circling back — action items recap: we'll send pricing; Priya will run EU perf baselines; Synergy will share prompt set; Emily will confirm compliance docs.
[09:03] Dr. Lina: sounds good. any blockers from your side?
[09:07] Jordan: none immediate. once we share the pricing and SE runs the tests you should have enough to make a procurement decision.
[09:13] Samir: one last technical ask — will Redwood support staged model swaps across routes (e.g., low-latency route pinned to quantized v1, fallback to higher-precision v2)?
[09:23] Priya: yes — routing policies let you pin route-specific model variants and fallbacks; it can also route by policy like latency vs cost.
[09:30] (small pause)
[09:33] Noah: okay we'll target internal review by 3/10 and then follow-up with questions.
[09:38] Jordan: perfect. we'll leave a time window to schedule the deep dive in mid-March. thanks all for the time.

[09:52] -- Meeting ends --

Post-meeting notes (auto): Redwood to include APAC burst pricing, EU private pilot timeline, SSO/KMS/retention capability notes. Customer wants baseline tests against their prompt set. Procurement timeline ~2 weeks internal review.
